item.title: Iron limitation reduces diatom carbon flow to bacteria through shifts in exometabolite consumption.
item.author: Gilbert NE, Coffey NR, McCall N, Kimbrel JA, Carlson CA, Halewood E, Ramon CE, Diep P, Weber PK, Mayali X, Boiteau RM, Stuart RK.
item.description:
Iron is required for photosynthesis and thus affects carbon fixation rates in widespread aquatic regions where availability is limited. Turnover of aquatic photosynthetically derived fixed carbon is largely constrained by bacterial activity, but it is unknown how algal iron limitation alters dissolved organic matter composition and subsequent processing through the microbial loop. We examined a bacterial community dependent on carbon from the diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum to investigate how iron limitation alters bacterial carbon processing. By quantifying activity at single-cell-resolution with nanoSIMS, we found that iron limitation led to a 43% reduction in carbon-fixation but an 80% reduction in carbon transfer into bacterial biomass. item.title: Ecological and evolutionary dynamics of chlamydiae endosymbionts in social amoeba host communities.
item.author: DuBose JG, Fiedorek P, Hoogshagen M, Clark D, Nolan A, Gerner H, Nguyen P, Gibbs K, Haselkorn TS.
item.description:
Endosymbiotic interactions have played fundamental roles in shaping the evolution of complex eukaryotes. However, how ecological processes shape endosymbioses that are still segregating in host populations have been less described. Here, we characterize the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of chlamydiae bacterial endosymbionts in dictyostelid social amoeba host communities. Our survey of over 1400 host isolates from across a 1200 km range revealed 41 unique chlamydiae haplotypes across 11 different host species, the prevalence of which significantly varied across host species and sampling locations. item.title: RNA viruses as drivers of rapid diatom succession within a single bloom event.
item.author: Mellijor JL, Tennenbuam-Azulai Y, Spungin D, Avrahami Y, Vardi A, Frada MJ, Kranzler CF.
item.description:
Diatoms frequently dominate seasonal phytoplankton blooms and contribute ~40% of marine primary production. Viruses drive phytoplankton mortality and bloom collapse, yet how viruses regulate diatom bloom dynamics is not well resolved. Here, using quantitative metatranscriptomics, we tracked temporal patterns of diatoms and associated viruses at near-daily resolution during the spring bloom in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea. We captured distinct phases and rapid restructuring within both the diatom community and cell-associated virosphere. Diatom transcriptional profiling indicated activation of stress and death pathways prior to taxon-specific demise. item.title: Multilayered network analysis reveals the centrality of newly discovered Nucleocytoviricota in wastewater treatment plant communities.
item.author: Lücking D, Manzano-Marín A, Willemsen A.
item.description:
Viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are remarkable entities due to their exceptionally large genomes and complex gene repertoires, which blur the lines between viral and cellular life. Previous research has leveraged computational approaches to map their extensive diversity. item.title: Nanoscale pesticide delivery suppresses pathogens and enriches beneficial microbiomes for safer crop protection.
item.author: Luo M, Dong M, Qiao H, Jin D, Chang S, Ullah F, Yin M, Shen J, Yin Y, Yan S.
item.description:
Nanocarrier-based pesticide delivery platforms substantially boost agrochemical utilization efficiency, yet their cascading ecological repercussions for rhizosphere and soil microbial ecology remain insufficiently understood. Here, a star polycation (SPc) nanocarrier was employed to construct a matrine nano-formulation (MT@SPc) with typical nano-pesticide characteristics. MT@SPc and commercial matrine formulation (MT SL) were employed as representative systems to further evaluate their impacts on rhizosphere and soil microbial ecosystems. Compared with MT SL, MT@SPc reshaped rhizosphere microbial communities by suppressing phytopathogens and promoting the enrichment of beneficial bacteria. item.title: Contrasting edaphic and land-use signatures of microbial phosphorus mobilisation and accumulation genes.
item.author: Du M, Xue P, Minasny B, Tang Y, Tran TKA, McBratney A.
item.description:
Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient that constrains productivity across many terrestrial ecosystems. Soil microorganisms regulate P transformation through distinct functional strategies, yet how these strategies vary with land use and environmental conditions across chronically P-impoverished landscapes remains poorly understood. Here, we combined 268 soil metagenomes from natural, pasture, and cropland systems across Australia with genome-resolved analyses of 1,077 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). Results revealed contrasting genomic distributions among P-cycling strategies. P accumulation genes were widely distributed across bacterial phylogeny, whereas mineralization gene and solubilisation gene were concentrated within specific lineages. item.title: Ecophysiology of the cosmopolitan nitrite-oxidising genus Candidatus Nitromaricola.
item.author: Stuehrenberg J, von Arx JN, Kitzinger K, Lavik G, Littmann S, Marchant HK, Milucka J, Orellana LH, Kuypers MMM.
item.description:
The majority of marine nitrite-oxidising bacteria (NOB) belong to three uncultured genera within the Nitrospinaceae family and thus the ecophysiology of these main nitrate producing microorganisms in the ocean remains poorly resolved. Here, we report on the environmental characterization of one of these genera, which we name Candidatus Nitromaricola. A single species within this genus, Candidatus Nitromaricola pontica, comprises >95% of the nitrite-oxidising community in the permanently stratified Black Sea. This provided a unique opportunity to study this globally abundant genus in situ, across pronounced environmental gradients of oxygen and inorganic nitrogen concentrations. We show that Ca. item.title: Fungi are overlooked dimethylsulfoniopropionate degraders in marine environments.
item.author: Liu GL, Zhang M, Song JZ, Wang Y, Zhang ZL, Zhang N, Zheng FH, Gu ZT, Zhu T, Honi U, Storer I, Breyer E, Pullin O, Fredriksson A, Bidula S, Baltar F, Todd JD, Zhang YZ, Li CY.
item.description:
Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a key marine organosulfur compound, whose microbial catabolism is critical to global sulfur cycling and is the major source of the climate-active gas dimethyl sulfide (DMS). Research has focused on bacterial and algal DMSP catabolism, potentially overlooking the importance of fungi. Here, we vastly extend the known diversity of fungi that cleave DMSP to DMS, showing that many lacked known DMSP lyases, and Pezizomycotina members were most active. The marine-derived yeast-like fungus Aureobasidium melanogenum imported DMSP for osmoprotection, and assimilated it via a previously unreported and efficient cupin-family cytoplasmic DMSP lyase, termed DddF. item.title: Community composition drives metabolic competition and Staphylococcus aureus colonization resistance in synthetic nasal communities.
item.author: Navarro-Diaz M, Bertram K, Göbel L, Camus L, Ham S, Angenent LT, Gomez JAV, Heilbronner S, Stincone P, Rapp J, Petras D, Link H.
item.description:
The human nasal microbiome is a low-diversity ecosystem whose assembly principles and mechanisms of colonization resistance remain poorly understood. Staphylococcus aureus is a member of the nasal microbiome of some individuals with variable abundance. We hypothesized that nutritional competition, strain-level diversity, and nutrient availability shape community stability and the ability of commensal species to inhibit S. aureus. To test this, we constructed 50 defined synthetic communities inoculated with 5 to 10 representative human nasal bacterial species differing in strain and species composition and tracked their compositional changes across serial passages, S. aureus growth, metabolic profiles, and nutritional interactions.
